messages.content: I need to set up a Boston work trip. The committee dinner is Thursday at 6:30 p.m., meetings run Friday from 8:30 to 5:00, and my rights roundtable ends Saturday at 1:00. I would be flying alone from Denver.
What dates are these, and where in Boston are the dinner and meetings? I can compare a Thursday arrival with an earlier arrival and check both Saturday and Sunday returns.
The dinner is Thursday, June 11, and the roundtable is Saturday, June 13. Everything is at the Boston Park Plaza. I would rather not add Wednesday unless Thursday is genuinely too tight.

A same-day arrival can work, but I would want you at the hotel by about 5:00 p.m. That leaves time for the airport transfer, check-in, and a buffer before dinner. I’ll look for morning Denver departures that reach Boston no later than roughly 3:30 p.m. local time. Do you want only nonstop flights, or should I include a connection if it materially improves the schedule or price?
Show me the sensible nonstop and one-stop choices. I’ll have one carry-on and one checked bag. For the return, I can leave Saturday if I’m not racing straight from the roundtable.

The strongest Thursday nonstop leaves Denver at 7:05 a.m. and reaches Boston at 12:50 p.m. The displayed round-trip fare with a Saturday return is $684 before any checked-bag charge. From Logan, allow about 25 to 45 minutes by taxi or rideshare to the Park Plaza, with more time in heavy traffic. Even allowing 30 minutes to collect the bag, you would likely reach the hotel between 1:50 and 2:30 p.m., giving you about four hours before dinner. A one-stop itinerary leaves at 6:20 a.m., connects in Chicago for 58 minutes, and arrives at 2:18 p.m. for $556 round trip. That still works on paper, but one delay could erase most of the margin.
The nonstop is worth the extra money for this schedule. What are the Saturday returns after 1:00? Include the time needed to get out of the meeting, retrieve my bag, and reach Logan.

There are two practical Saturday nonstops. The first departs Boston at 5:10 p.m. and arrives Denver at 7:42 p.m.; the second leaves at 7:35 p.m. and arrives at 10:08 p.m. The 5:10 flight is possible but compressed: leave the roundtable at 1:00, allow 15 minutes for final conversations, retrieve stored luggage by 1:30, and leave the hotel around 1:40. With normal traffic you could reach Logan near 2:10, about three hours before departure, but a delayed session or severe traffic would reduce that cushion. The 7:35 flight gives ample room for the same sequence and is included in the $684 fare.
Is there a Sunday option that is meaningfully cheaper? I’m comparing two hotel nights and the later Saturday flight against three nights and a less tiring return.

Yes. Returning Sunday at 11:20 a.m. nonstop, arriving Denver at 1:52 p.m., brings the displayed airfare down to $598. Another Sunday nonstop leaves at 3:45 p.m. and arrives at 6:17 p.m.; that itinerary is $626. Both require a third hotel night. I’ll compare the total trip cost rather than airfare alone.
Please do. I need a quiet standard room for one person, and I don’t need breakfast included. Compare the Park Plaza with two nearby alternatives that are genuinely walkable at 8:00 in the morning.

For June 11-13, the Park Plaza shows a standard king at $319 per night and $748 total after estimated taxes and the mandatory destination charge. Staying at the venue removes the Friday and Saturday commute. The Revere Hotel, about a six-minute walk, shows a king room at $287 nightly and $674 total. The Courtyard Boston Downtown, about nine minutes on foot, shows a king at $251 nightly and $589 total. None of these totals includes breakfast. For June 11-14, the corresponding estimated totals are $1,112 at the Park Plaza, $1,001 at the Revere, and $875 at the Courtyard.
Put airfare and lodging together. Also account for the fact that I can store my bag at the hotel Saturday after checkout.

The two-night totals with the Thursday outbound and Saturday 7:35 p.m. nonstop are: Park Plaza $1,432, Revere $1,358, and Courtyard $1,273. The three-night totals with the Sunday 11:20 a.m. nonstop are: Park Plaza $1,710, Revere $1,599, and Courtyard $1,473. These figures combine displayed airfare and lodging only; add the applicable checked-bag fee and local airport transportation. On Saturday, all three hotels indicate luggage storage is available after checkout, but complimentary storage should be confirmed with the property before booking.
The Courtyard saves enough to consider, but tell me what the walk is like and whether staying there creates any issue for the Thursday dinner.

The Courtyard is roughly 0.5 mile from the Park Plaza, generally a 9- to 12-minute walk along city streets. For Thursday, a 12:50 p.m. flight arrival should put you at the hotel around 2:00 to 2:40 p.m. After check-in, leaving by 6:10 gives you comfortable time to walk to the 6:30 dinner. Friday, leaving around 8:05 should get you to the Park Plaza before the 8:30 start. The main tradeoff is carrying weather gear and making the walk twice on Friday plus once Saturday morning, rather than using elevators within the venue.
I’ll stay at the Park Plaza for two nights. The convenience matters during the Friday schedule. Keep the Saturday 7:35 flight, provided the post-roundtable timing is comfortable.

That combination is comfortable. On Saturday, check out before the roundtable and leave your checked bag with the bell desk. When the session ends at 1:00, you can allow 30 to 45 minutes for conversations, collect the bag by about 2:00, and still have more than five hours before the 7:35 departure. A car leaving the hotel at 4:30 would normally reach Logan around 5:00 to 5:20, leaving over two hours at the airport. You also have room to depart earlier if traffic conditions worsen.
Can you give me the complete record, including the Thursday airport margin and what is not yet verified? Don’t book anything yet.

Provisional Boston trip record for Elena Ruiz, traveling alone: Thursday, June 11, depart Denver at 7:05 a.m. on the selected nonstop and arrive Boston at 12:50 p.m. After collecting one checked bag, use a taxi or rideshare to the Boston Park Plaza and target hotel arrival between 1:50 and 2:30 p.m. This leaves about four hours before the 6:30 p.m. committee dinner at the hotel. Stay in one standard king room at the Boston Park Plaza for two nights, checking in June 11 and checking out Saturday, June 13. Displayed lodging total is $748, including estimated taxes and the mandatory destination charge; breakfast is not included. Friday sessions run at the hotel from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. On Saturday, check out before the rights roundtable, store the checked bag with the bell desk, and attend the session through 1:00 p.m. Allow time afterward for conversations and retrieve the bag by about 2:00. Leave for Logan around 4:30, adjusting earlier for traffic, for the selected 7:35 p.m. nonstop to Denver, arriving at 10:08 p.m. Displayed round-trip airfare is $684, and the combined displayed airfare and hotel estimate is $1,432 before checked-bag fees and ground transportation. Nothing has been booked. Before purchase, verify live flight and room inventory, flight numbers, operating carriers, terminals, exact fare rules, baggage charges, seat availability, the final hotel tax and destination-charge breakdown, room type and bed guarantee, cancellation terms, check-in time, and complimentary Saturday luggage storage. Also recheck Logan travel time and any major local traffic or transit disruptions shortly before departure.
